_comment: Read-only release artifact compiled into the binary with include_bytes!.
It is not a user setting and is never fetched at runtime.
An entry may be added only after all five approval reports in section 9.5 of
docs/UBUNTU_TF_CARD_VIDEO_PIPELINE_IMPLEMENTATION.md exist in versioned release
evidence: representative quality corpus, throughput/CPU/memory/disk, stereo/CV
domain, encoder distribution + legal review, and playback compatibility.
Only their digests belong here; the reports themselves stay in release evidence.
'entries' is deliberately empty. The HEVC V1 parameters (libx265 preset=slow,
CRF 20 for MJPEG sources and CRF 18 for H.264 sources) are candidates and have
no approval reports yet, so normalization stays capability-unavailable rather
than deriving video against an unreviewed profile.
Each entry has the shape:
"quality_variant": "mjpeg_crf20" | "h264_crf18" | "h264_crf16_retry",
"profile_revision": "sha256:<64 lowercase hex>",
"encoder_compatibility_class": "x265-software-hevc-main-8bit-v1",
"approved_at": "<RFC 3339>",
"reports": {
"quality_corpus": "sha256:...",
"throughput_resource": "sha256:...",
"stereo_cv": "sha256:...",
"encoder_distribution_legal_review": "sha256:...",
"playback_compatibility": "sha256:..."
The loader rebuilds the named variant from code, recomputes its canonical
revision, and rejects the entry when the two disagree. Changing any profile
parameter therefore invalidates its approval instead of silently inheriting it.
